profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC8 sits at 22190 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." A third-party data center aggregator separately reports 108 megawatts specifically for LC8, a figure this profile notes as unconfirmed by the operator rather than adopting as fact. CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available, a campus-wide total not broken out by individual building. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available." CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide and over 6,000 megawatts of further expansion potential, figures CloudHQ discloses on its own homepage alongside a stated 5.2-gigawatt global data center inventory.

sources.title: DataCenterMap, Ashburn Virginia Data Centers Listing (LC8 108MW aggregator figure)

profile.capacity_note: DataCenterMap gives 108 MW for this building, a single aggregator figure, not confirmed by the operator, so not applied to critical_it_mw. Per CloudHQs own current page for the LC Campus (tier-1 operator source, https://cloudhq.com/campus/lc-campus/), this campus is in the heart of Ashburn, Virginia, directly off Loudoun County Parkway, and totals about 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 MW of total critical IT load across fourteen data centers, with 756 MW available critical load, as of this sessions retrieval. Because this is a fourteen-building campus total, it is not applied to any individual rows critical_it_mw.
profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 38 (CloudHQ VA missing-address campaign): preferred a distinguishing datacenterHawk address over a Baxtel figure shared with two neighboring rows, refreshed company history from the operators own about and founder pages, flagged a second CloudHQ name collision on Wikipedia not present in a prior sessions notes. research_status remains complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CloudHQ, the data center operator, was established in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, per the operators own current about page (cloudhq.com/about/) fetched fresh this session. Fateh previously served as CEO and co-founder of DuPont Fabros Technology, a data center company that sold for 7.8 billion dollars in 2017, and has built and operated more than 700 MW of data center capacity across his career, per CloudHQs own founder page (cloudhq.com/learn-about-our-founder/), also fetched fresh this session. CloudHQ operates as part of the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated companies CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development, per the operators own about page. The company maintains three regional headquarters, a global headquarters in Washington DC, an EMEA headquarters in London, and an APAC headquarters in Singapore. Per the operators own current about page, CloudHQ now describes 23 global campuses, more than 1,380 MW of contracted critical IT load with more than 6,000 MW of expansion potential, more than 30 million square feet of global data center portfolio, and more than 330 employees. A prior research pass on these rows had already flagged that the domain cloudhq.net resolves to an unrelated Google Workspace and Gmail backup software company, not this data center operator, and correctly redirected to cloudhq.com. This session found a second, separate name collision worth flagging for a future researcher: the Wikipedia article at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CloudHQ describes yet another different, unrelated company, a cloud data synchronization tool for Google Workspace founded in 2011 by Senad Dizdar and based in San Francisco, not this Ashburn and Manassas Virginia data center operator founded by Hossein Fateh. That Wikipedia article was checked this session and found not to apply, so it is not used or cited as a source here, and no Wikipedia sourced company history is included in this reading. This specific row, LC8, is described by CloudHQs own LC Campus page context as a three story facility totaling roughly 805,600 square feet, located adjacent to CloudHQs LC4 facility, per Baxtels dedicated LC8 page. Two aggregators disagree on this buildings specific street number: Baxtels own dedicated LC8 page gives 22210 Loudoun County Parkway, the same figure Baxtel separately assigns to neighboring LC9 and LC10, while datacenterHawks dedicated LC8 listing gives a distinct 22190 Loudoun County Parkway. Because the datacenterHawk figure is the one that actually distinguishes this row from its LC9 and LC10 neighbors, it is preferred here, with Baxtels competing, shared figure flagged rather than silently dropped.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC8 is one building in a fourteen-building campus totaling 1,256 megawatts of critical IT load in Ashburn, Virginia, the world's densest data center corridor. The operator publishes only a campus-wide capacity figure, not a breakdown by building. A third-party aggregator reports 108 megawatts specifically for LC8, unconfirmed by CloudHQ, which if accurate would represent roughly 2,700 racks at the common 40 kilowatt-per-rack AI training density, or roughly 900 eight-GPU accelerator units at 120 kilowatts per unit.

The LC Campus sits directly off Loudoun County Parkway in Ashburn, where dozens of hyperscale operators compete within miles of each other. Virginia's 23 published data center facilities collectively account for 1,375 megawatts of known capacity. The full LC Campus, at 1,256 megawatts across fourteen buildings, represents a single operator's large installed base and dominates Virginia's published capacity profile, though most of Virginia's 326 mapped facilities publish no figures.

CloudHQ states 756 megawatts of available capacity across the full LC Campus as of publication, suggesting growth headroom. The operator does not name its power utility in published materials; Dominion Energy is the primary utility across Loudoun County. The grid constraint on further scaling this campus remains unpublished.
